head: claude/session-invokable-actions-ci-settled
title: ci-settled: a session-invokable CI waiter, so the runner polls instead of the session
body:
## What

A session-invokable GitHub Action that does the **waiting** so a session does not.

`api.github.com` returns **HTTP 403** from inside a Claude Code sandbox — re-confirmed live in this session (2026-09-02), against a **200** from `https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/health` in the same shell, so the block is specific to the GitHub API and not to egress in general. The consequence is the cost this PR removes: a session **cannot** script a CI poller, so the only way to learn whether its PR's suite has finished is to call `mcp__github__pull_request_read` again, and again, and again — each call spending context to be told *still running*.

## How

- **`.github/workflows/ci-settled.yml`** — push relay on `automation/ci-watch/**` (the `pr-opener.yml` / `board-post.yml` shape, chosen because `issue_write` 403s for exactly the sessions that need this). It polls on the runner and commits one compact result to `automation/ci-results/<name>.json`.
- **`scripts/ops/ci_settle.py`** — the grader. Seven states, kept apart deliberately.
- **`scripts/ops/ci_settled.sh`** — one command: `scripts/ops/ci_settled.sh <PR> [minutes]`.
- **`tests/test_ci_settle.py`** — 25 tests; the same assertions also live behind `--self-test`, which the workflow runs *before* trusting the grader.

## The payload is one read, not four

It carries `mergeable_state` (with a plain-English note), the deduped check roll-up, unresolved review threads, and — when red — a **bounded** excerpt of the failing job log. That last one matters: without it a red verdict still costs a `get_job_logs` call returning an entire job log.

## Never collapsed

- **zero check runs → `no_checks`, NEVER `green`.** This is the trap `CLAUDE.md` records costing two sessions ~10 minutes each.
- **`conflict` is reported ahead of `no_checks`**, because a dirty merge ref is the *cause* of the emptiness, not a separate symptom.
- **`cancelled` is its own state** — it produced no verdict, and this repo runs `cancel-in-progress: true` on its required checks, so grading it green would be a false pass.
- **`unreadable` is never folded into `no_checks`** — *we could not look* and *we looked and found nothing* are opposite facts. Its counts are `null`, not `0`.
- **A timeout reports `pending`** — *we* stopped waiting; CI did not stop.

## It never touches the PR it is watching

The request is built with git plumbing on top of `origin/main` and pushed to a throwaway `automation/ciwatch-<name>` branch. A request committed onto the watched branch would add a commit to the PR head, re-trigger the very run being waited on, and move the head out from under the answer.

## Blast radius

Reports only. Cannot merge, cannot push to `main`, cannot open or close anything, never reaches `src/`, `config/`, a unit file, or either VM. Its one write is a result file on a branch whose name it was handed.

## Verification

- `scripts/ops/ci_settle.py --self-test` → OK (25 assertions)
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_ci_settle.py` → **25 passed** (pytest was absent from the container; installed to run them)
- `scripts/ci/check_workflow_catalog.py --all` → OK, 130 workflows
- **End-to-end dispatch proof against this very PR** — posted as a comment below once the relay has run. A workflow that has never actually run is precisely the *looks-armed-and-is-not* state this repo has been bitten by.
